title: U.S. Senate · Virginia

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and incumbent Mark Warner advanced unopposed. Bert Mizusawa won the Republican primary on August 4, 2026 with 51.5% of the vote, defeating David Williams (28.9%) and Kim Farington (19.6%).
Independent candidate Mark Moran withdrew from the general election and is not on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot.

summary.text: Mark Warner is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator from Virginia, first elected in 2008 and previously Governor of Virginia from 2002 to 2006. He is running for re-election, citing work on infrastructure investment, domestic manufacturing, health care costs, and his role on the Senate Intelligence Committee.

background.text: Born in Indianapolis, Indiana in 1954; earned a bachelor's degree in political science from George Washington University and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 1980.
Worked as a staffer for Sen. Chris Dodd, served as Virginia Democratic Party chair, and co-founded the cell phone company that became Nextel.
Served as Governor of Virginia from 2002 to 2006 before his election to the U.S. Senate.

priorities.text: Says he has worked to strengthen America's economy and "spearheaded the largest infrastructure investments in half a century" and expanded Virginia's domestic manufacturing.
Cites work to lower health care costs for Virginia families.

Cites his work on the Senate Intelligence Committee, where he served as chairman in 2021-2022 and serves as vice chairman in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), as central to "protecting the highest levels of America's national security."

record.text: Serves on the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Securities, Insurance, and Investment); the Committee on Finance; the Committee on Rules and Administration; the Select Committee on Intelligence (Vice Chairman); and the Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Bert Mizusawa
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 51.5% of the vote

summary.text: Bert Mizusawa is a retired U.S. Army major general and the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate. He describes 41 years of military service including four combat tours, prior service as a Senate professional staff member, and as Deputy Under Secretary of the Army and senior advisor at the CIA.

background.text: Retired U.S. Army major general with 41 years of service, including four combat tours; West Point valedictorian and Harvard Law graduate; recipient of a Silver Star for valor.
Previously served as a professional staff member in the U.S. Senate, as Deputy Under Secretary of the Army, and as a senior advisor at the CIA.
Small business owner; shares seven children and four grandchildren with his wife Amy.

priorities.text: Says he will be an "authoritative voice on national security policy and efficient defense spending" as a combat veteran in the Senate.
priorities.quote: Will be av respected, authoritative voice on national security policy and efficient defense spending. Combat veteran in US Senate.

priorities.text: Says the country is "a nation of laws" that must "enforce the law uniformly."
priorities.quote: We are a nation of laws and must enforce the law uniformly
